title: JavaScript Code Lab: Solve & Learn
description: Sharpen your JavaScript skills with four hands-on coding challenges! From reversing strings to checking palindromes, write real code in an interactive editor, run test cases, and learn fundamental programming concepts. Perfect for beginners and intermediate coders preparing for coding interviews and competitive programming.
learning_objectives: Write JavaScript functions that solve common algorithmic problems
Understand string manipulation techniques including reversal and palindrome detection
Apply conditional logic and loops to implement FizzBuzz-style branching problems
Use recursion and iterative approaches to calculate mathematical sequences like factorials
Develop debugging and test-driven thinking by validating code against multiple test cases

challenges.title: Reverse a String
challenges.description: Write a function that takes a string as input and returns the string reversed. Do not use the built-in reverse() method -- implement the logic yourself using a loop or recursion.
hints: You can iterate through the string from the last character to the first and build a new string
Try using a for loop that starts at input.length - 1 and decrements to 0
Alternatively, you can split the string into an array of characters, reverse the array, and join it back

examples.explanation: The characters h-e-l-l-o are reversed to o-l-l-e-h
Note that the capital N moves to the end, preserving the original casing of each character

challenges.title: FizzBuzz
challenges.description: Write a function that takes a number n as input and returns a string with numbers from 1 to n separated by commas. But for multiples of 3, use 'Fizz' instead of the number; for multiples of 5, use 'Buzz'; and for multiples of both 3 and 5, use 'FizzBuzz'.
hints: Use a for loop from 1 to n and check divisibility with the modulo operator (%)
Important: Check for divisibility by both 3 AND 5 first (i % 15 === 0), before checking 3 or 5 individually
Build an array of results and join them with commas at the end using .join(',')

examples.explanation: 1 and 2 are printed as-is. 3 is a multiple of 3, so it becomes 'Fizz'. 4 is printed. 5 is a multiple of 5, so it becomes 'Buzz'.
15 is divisible by both 3 and 5, so it becomes 'FizzBuzz'. This is the classic interview problem!

challenges.title: Calculate Factorial
challenges.description: Write a function that takes a non-negative integer n as input and returns its factorial (n!). The factorial of n is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n. By definition, 0! = 1.
hints: You can solve this iteratively using a loop: multiply a running product from 1 up to n
Alternatively, use recursion: factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1), with factorial(0) = 1 as the base case

examples.explanation: 5! = 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 120. The factorial function grows very quickly!
By mathematical convention, 0! is defined as 1. This is important for combinatorics and probability formulas.

challenges.title: Palindrome Check
challenges.description: Write a function that takes a string as input and returns 'true' if it is a palindrome and 'false' otherwise. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Ignore case differences (treat uppercase and lowercase as equal) and ignore spaces.

test_cases.input: Was It A Rat I Saw

hints: First, convert the string to lowercase and remove all spaces to normalise it
Then compare the cleaned string with its reverse
You can also use a two-pointer approach: compare characters from the start and end, moving inward

examples.explanation: 'madam' reads the same forwards (m-a-d-a-m) and backwards (m-a-d-a-m), so it is a palindrome.
After converting to lowercase and removing spaces, 'racecar' is a palindrome. The function ignores case and whitespace.

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Choose a coding challenge from the four available problems, starting from easier to harder
Read the problem description, examples, and expected input/output format carefully
Write your JavaScript solution in the code editor provided
Click 'Run Tests' to execute your code against all test cases and see which ones pass
If some tests fail, review the error messages, use the hints, and refine your solution
Each challenge is worth 100 points -- earn full points by passing all test cases
tips: Read the examples first to understand exactly what the function should return
Start with the Reverse String challenge -- it is the most straightforward and builds confidence
For FizzBuzz, always check the 'both 3 and 5' condition before checking 3 or 5 individually
The Factorial problem can be solved with either a loop or recursion -- both approaches work
For Palindrome Check, remember to normalise the string (lowercase, remove spaces) before comparing
Use console.log() inside your function to debug and trace variable values during testing

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: Notice how each decision here requires weighing multiple options. Strategic thinkers pause before choosing — what's the long-term implication of each answer?
